text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Nguyen Cong Tan told the National Assembly that 35.6 percent of the country's land mass will be covered by forest by 2000.
-- A 10-day trial of 22 alleged members of an international drug trafficking ring, including senior police officers, will open in Hanoi on May 2.
-- Vietnam's goverment has agreed to allow 100 percent foreign-invested enterprises to carry forward losses incurred before 1997 to their next fiscal year for tax purposes.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet told the ASEAN labour ministers' meeting that Vietnam hopes to receive more help from other countries to improve labour quality and workers' skills.
-- The communist parties of Vietnam and Russia are planning to strengthen relations.
-- Hanoi has launched campaign to kill rats in the city area.
-- Vietnam has set fines for non-state businesses which fail to re-register their activities.
-- Norwegian Coorperation and Development Minister Kari Nordheim Larsen said Norway might grant Vietnam a preferential credit of $15 million for Vietnam in 1997.
